text.text_excerpt: After moving to New Orleans almost 2 years ago, it still blows my mind that I can find the most delicious foods in the most random places. We've Got Soul is now a solid part of Carrollton Station, a bar in the East Carollton area. They serve up weekly rotating dishes Thursday through Sunday, usually from 5pm-midnight. During football season, if there's an afternoon Saints game, they generally open up shop earlier too. My routine: Grab a drink from the bar, score a table outside in the fenced-in backyard area, and start crossing my fingers that We've Got Soul has Boudin Eggrolls on their bar menu that week. My mouth is watering now just thinking about them. Pork Chops and Brisket are more ...

We've Got Soul is absolutely incredible. Let's start with the food... ughhh the food!! It is always delicious, rich, and unique. I've had plenty of soul food in my life, but this place gives it a new meaning and some new flavor profiles. I've been more times than I have been able to keep track of, but last night I had the best green beans of my life. They were crispy Memphis dry rub green beans, and my girlfriend and I poured the leftover juice from our also amazing chargrilled mussels on them. The menu changes every week, but some all time standouts for me have been the pan-seared salmon, the lemon butter chicken thighs, and the root beer glazed pork chop recently. Those are entrees, but...

Great grub in one of my favorite bars in town. I was skeptical when it landed, because We've Got Soul replaced a tried and true (and cheap) bar kitchen turning out baskets of chicken tenders and fries. However, once over the shock I am all in for We've Got Soul. The menu changes weekly - which keeps things varied. You pick one of three mains and get two of four side items for the princely sum of $16. More than a chicken basket but so worth it. The food is excellent great flavor and a nice mix of the decadent (oxtail) to the moderately ok (mahi-mahi and salmon recently - of course with a touch of sauce to negate any nutritional properties).
